note: THE RETENTION PROOF. Nothing here is quoted from a record and re-labelled as evidence: every observed figure was produced by re-running this repository's real generator against the pinned base, and every committed figure it is compared against was read from the record that was gated when the bytes were first made. A disagreement anywhere is recorded as a DIFFERS row and this stage exits non-zero; a census is never adjusted until it matches. No GLB was retained: the wave passes run census-only and the shipped replay hashes its bytes and drops them.

adjudicatedContractNote.note: DERIVED, NOT ASSERTED. Every key path of each committed record below was enumerated and every 64-hex string located. The five wave censuses carry NO per-building plan-hash artifact: their only plan-hash key is the scalar `uniquePlanHashCount`, so an acceptance criterion phrased as a comparison against 'committed wave census plan hashes' has no per-building artifact to compare against. The replay below therefore proves the same claim through three real instruments instead, and the cardinality of the replayed per-building hash SET is compared against each committed `uniquePlanHashCount` integer.

generatorIdentity.note: Recorded on BOTH sides of every comparison below: the same generator identity produced the committed bytes and the replayed ones, and a version move would be visible here rather than hidden in a checksum.

crossWaveHashComparisonNote: A V3 plan hash covers the wave's seed, generated instant and tool identity as well as the sourced polygon. The six wave seeds are committed constants and they differ, so plan hashes are NOT comparable across waves and no comparison here crosses a wave boundary. Every wave is replayed with its OWN profile; the only cross-wave statement made anywhere is that plan-stage REFUSAL is a function of the sourced polygon alone, which is a statement about counts and is tested by `distributions.json`, not by hashes.

waveAggregateReplay.note: Each generated wave re-run through `materializeMidtownCoreV3Cells` with `retain: "census-only"` and that wave's OWN committed census profile, over the ledger cells the wave owns. `materializedBuildingCount` and `tierCollapseAbsentSetbackCount` are ASSET-stage facts, so they are produced by running the asset writer rather than derived from the plan stage plus a committed correction.

waves.note: Wave w00 committed no wave-scale census. Its per-building plan hashes are replayed in `block835PlanReplay`, which is a STRONGER comparison than any aggregate: hash for hash rather than count against count.

hashSpace.note: The committed record carries only a cardinality. This is the replayed SET whose cardinality it claims to be, rebuilt one plan hash per materialized building with this wave's own seed, generated instant and tool identity.

stageBoundary.note: `waveRefusals` is the PLAN stage and `wave.refusalsByCode` is the ASSET stage, which is the plan stage plus the writer's own stop codes. This checks the committed record against itself, and the replayed plan-stage partition against the committed plan-stage map.

block835PlanReplay.note: Wave w00 committed no wave-scale census, so there is no aggregate to reconcile. What it DOES commit — uniquely in this repository — is a per-building plan hash for each of its 14 buildings, in three independent records. Each is replayed through the reference package's own grammar entrypoint and compared hash for hash. The `-v3t` census reports the same hashes as `-v3` (`summary.planHashesUnchangedFromV3`), and `-v3e` differs on exactly the one building carrying a cited style override.

shippedAssetByteReplay.note: BYTE IDENTITY, not count agreement. Every shipped GLB of every wave is regenerated with that wave's SHIPPED profile and its SHA-256 is compared against the committed checksum record. This is the property the retain-versus-regenerate decision in ADR 0046 rests on.

perBuildingPlanHashCorollary.note: `writeCanonicalGlb` writes `planHashSha256` into every asset's metadata, so a byte-identical GLB is only obtainable from an identical plan hash. Byte identity across the shipped set is therefore ALSO a per-building plan-hash identity proof — and outside Block 835's fourteen buildings it is the ONLY one available, because no wave census commits per-building hashes to compare against.
perBuildingPlanHashCorollary.mechanism: asset metadata field `planHashSha256`, written by writeCanonicalGlb and covered by the artifact SHA-256

waves.note: Wave w00 has no payload inventory under data/: its bytes are git-tracked, so the committed pin is the emitted release's own assemblies.json. The shipped release promotes the manhattan-esb-block-reference-20260811-v3e package unchanged, so the same bytes are compared against BOTH the shipped pin and the input package manifest.

closedLoop.note: Wave w00 is the only wave whose payload bytes are git-tracked, so its loop closes on three independent sides rather than two: the bytes this run regenerated, the checksum the committed manifest declares, and the SHA-256 of the file actually on disk. For the other five waves the payload directory is untracked by design, so the committed inventory is the only committed side and the comparison is regenerated-against-recorded.

verdict.statement: Regeneration is byte-exact on the SHIPPED set (498/498 GLBs match their committed SHA-256) and aggregate-exact on the GENERATED set (88,562 assets totalling 4,706,024,864 B reproduced as committed byte totals, per-wave). The generated set's per-asset bytes were dropped by the census-only wave passes and were never committed, so aggregate identity is the strongest claim available for it, and it is the claim made.
verdict.generatedSetGrain: aggregate-identical, per wave (counts, refusal maps, byte totals, triangle totals, plan-hash set cardinality)
